summary.headline: Manba Finance Q2 FY27 PAT rose 20% YoY to INR14 crores, NII up 40% to INR52 crores, AUM up 21% to INR1,811 crores.
summary.overview: Manba Finance reported Q2 FY27 net interest income of INR52 crores (up 40% YoY) and PAT of INR14 crores (up 20% YoY), with H1 NII of INR94 crores (up 39%) and H1 PAT of INR27 crores (up 28%). AUM reached INR1,811 crores at September 30, 2026, up 21% YoY, while GNPA improved to 2.96% and NNPA to 2.19%. Management said a rating upgrade to A minus stable from CARE and lower borrowing costs (average cost 10.14%) should support margins, and reiterated 30-35% AUM growth guidance for FY27 despite H1 growth of about 20%. The call was hosted by Antique Stock Broking and included mostly retail-investor questions.

segments.name: 2-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 83.10% of portfolio; main growth driver in the quarter, supported by dealer network expansion and new locations. Dealer base about 1,900-1,932 across 148 locations in 7 states.

segments.name: Top-up loans
segments.commentary: 5.70% of portfolio; secured against existing 2-wheeler customers, quoted IRR around 32%.

segments.name: 3-wheeler loans
segments.commentary: 3% of portfolio. Battery replacement loan for EV 3-wheelers launched about 2 months ago, limited to own customers and to be tested for 18 months.

segments.name: Used vehicle loans
segments.commentary: 1.60% of portfolio; used 2-wheeler loans quoted at 27-28% IRR, with 100-plus dealers added in the last 6 months.

segments.name: MSME LAP / small business loans
segments.commentary: Small business loan IRR about 27-28%, average ticket INR5 lakh, NPAs 3-4%. MSME LAP disbursement at INR2-2.5 crores per month, targeted at INR5 crores per month by January.

segments.name: Personal loans
segments.commentary: Unsecured, IRR similar to top-up (around 32%); being scaled cautiously through DSAs.

guidance_outlook: AUM and disbursement growth guidance for FY27 of 30-35%; management said H1 AUM growth was about 20% and H2 festive season should close the gap.
Management expects FY28 growth to continue but gave no numerical guidance.

Borrowing costs: about INR600 crores of high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; management expects about 25 bps overall impact in Q3-Q4 and a 50-75 bps reduction in cost of funds from the rating upgrade.
NIM concern raised by an analyst: prior guidance of 13-14% versus about 12.3% currently; management said NIM would not be hit by the RBI rate hike.
Capital from INR100 crore preferential issue expected by November 6, 2026; management expects capital to support growth for 4-6 quarters.
Interim dividend of INR0.25 per share declared for FY27 (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: INR100 crore preferential issue of equity and warrants; board approved in Q2, principal approval from NSE and BSE received, funds expected by November 6, 2026.

Operations in 148 locations across 7 states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Karnataka); about 16 offices added in the last year and 5-6 more small business loan branches planned this quarter.
Karnataka launched about 60 days before the call, with 100-plus dealers onboarded; Karnataka season expected in January.
Technology spend about INR2 crores per year with a 28-person tech team; disbursement turnaround cut from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeted same-day by end of year.
Employee base about 2,061, of which 1,100-plus in sales; 2.45 lakh+ live customers after adding about 32,330 in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Industry: 2-wheeler registrations about 53 lakh units in Q2, with August and September both record highs; September retail registrations up 32% YoY per FADA.
Management expects Diwali and Navratri season to lift H2 disbursements; said October alone added INR120 crores of new AUM after run-down.
Competition in 2-wheeler loans named as IDFC, L&T and regional players such as Berar; management claims about 15% market share in locations operating for 4+ years.
Bounce rate about 18-20%, with 7-8% of customers remaining in bounce across tenure, per management.
NTC (new-to-credit) customers about 40% of the book; LTV capped at 75% for them.

qa_highlights.question: Growth timeline for newer states (UP, MP, Rajasthan) given Gujarat and Maharashtra hold about half the dealer base.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Maharashtra and Gujarat dealer tie-ups are largely complete; new dealer additions are coming from Rajasthan, UP, MP and Karnataka, with 100-plus dealers onboarded in Karnataka in the first 60 days.

qa_highlights.question: How many quarters the INR100 crore raise will support growth, and FY27-28 growth guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Capital should support growth for 4-6 quarters; FY27 guidance is 30-35% growth, with H1 at about 20% and festive season in H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is 30-35% AUM growth achievable given H1 AUM growth of about INR98 crores, and any El Nino impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said October added INR120 crores of AUM and similar is expected in November; MSME LAP and small business loans, 5-6 new branches and 10-12 live BC partners were cited as additional drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Operating expenses up 28% YoY in Q2; drivers and cost optimisation.
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to 16 new offices in the last year, Karnataka expansion and seasonal sales hiring, and said YoY cost comparison is not a fair measure given the expansion; NIM, average cost and credit cost were said to be improving QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Further cost-of-funds reduction and NIM trajectory (guidance 13-14% vs 12.3% currently).
qa_highlights.answer: About INR600 crores of old high-cost borrowings to be repaid by March 2027; overall impact of about 25 bps expected in Q3-Q4, and new borrowings are at lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Share of NTC borrowers and delinquency comparison; used vehicle and high-yield products.
qa_highlights.answer: NTC share about 40%; behaviour broadly similar to other customers except those with CIBIL above 750. Used 2-wheeler IRR 27-28%, top-up and personal loan IRR about 32%.

risks_watch: AUM growth of 30-35% requires roughly INR400-450 crores of H2 additions versus H1 growth of about 20%; festive-season delivery is key.
Rising RBI repo rate versus management's expectation of 50-75 bps cost-of-funds reduction from the rating upgrade.
NIM at about 12.3% versus prior 13-14% guidance.
Operating expense growth of 28% YoY in Q2 with ongoing branch expansion.
Concentration in 2-wheeler (83.10%) and unsecured personal loans being scaled up; EV battery replacement product is untested.
Completion of the INR100 crore preferential issue by November 6, 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and funding costs, with management repeatedly citing festive-season momentum and the rating upgrade. Cautious on personal loans and the EV battery product, which are being tested slowly. Somewhat evasive on the NIM gap versus guidance and on the cost-growth question, which it deflected to expansion and QoQ trends.
